label: Origin-compatible deletion: a world lacking any given individual with shared origins kept near
definition: OriginCompatibleDeletion m Concrete I holds when, for every world v and every concrete individual x existing at v, some world u lacks x while every individual existing at both v and u has, at u, an origin near its origin at v. It is a claim about which worlds there are (a recombination or free-deletion plenitude restricted by origins), not about access: it mentions no access relation. Its extreme case is a world at which no individual exists, which satisfies the origin clause vacuously for every v and x. Example: OriginDeletion.Control.withEmpty. Counterexample: OriginToleranceIdentity.Control.faithful, where the only world lacking b is aMinus, which gives a the origin -1, far from its origin +1 at plus. Distinguished from OriginPlenitude, which realises near variations of the origin of an existing individual and never requires its absence, and from unrestricted Humean recombination, which also recombines distinct existents freely.
note: Analyst candidate commitment, unattributed; attribution deferred. It is not among the encoded origin-tolerance commitments (NearIsTolerance, OriginDeterminesAccess, OriginPlenitude, VariedOriginAt), which constrain the origins of existing individuals and are silent on existence. Whether a defender of origin tolerance accepts it, and whether metaphysical possibility satisfies it, are OPEN. Origins remain idle where an individual does not exist.
